newsitem.title: UK: Scot TV upbeat on Caledonian, record yr pft.
newsitem.headline: Scot TV upbeat on Caledonian, record yr pft.

text.p: Scottish Television Plc predicted on Tuesday that its recent Caledonian publishing acquisition would have a significant impact on 1997 results after reporting record profits for last year which accounted for one-off gains.

Pretax profits for the year ended December 31 were 61.2 million pounds ($99.64 million) including a 33.2 million gain from investment disposals. Stripping out that factor profits were up 40 percent at 28 million pounds. The total dividend was 18.7 pence.

Gus MacDonald, executive chairman, said in a statement the company was in a strong position to develop into a "broadly based Scottish media group" and added that the Caledonian business "will have a significant impact on our business and financial results in 1997.

"With good progress on integration the achievement of our initial cost saving targets are in prospect," he added. He said newspaper and advertising sales for the unit were in line with expectations and was positive for the broader outlook.

Total sales for the media group were 127.3 million pounds, including acquisitions, a rise of 29 percent. The group expects growth in the British economy despite the uncertainty ahead of the election due by May 22.
